Phoney War: Initial period of low activity in World War II.
This Macedonian Greek general, one of Alexander the Great's most trusted companions, retrieved his leader's body after his death and founded a new ruling dynasty in Egypt — who is he?
Ptolemy I Soter: Pharaoh of Egypt from 305 to 282 BC.
Taking office in December 1983, this Argentine lawyer and social democrat was the first democratically elected president after the country's military 'National Reorganization Process' — who was he?
Raúl Alfonsín: President of Argentina from 1983 to 1989.
Deposed in a 2017 coup after ruling Zimbabwe for 37 years as both prime minister and president, who was this revolutionary-turned-leader?
Robert Mugabe: Leader of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 2017.
In 2023 this German politician walked out of The Left to found a Eurosceptic populist party bearing her own name — which firebrand was she?

Depicted in reliefs at Ramesses III's mortuary temple, this mysterious maritime confederation was long blamed for Late Bronze Age raids on Egypt around 1200 BC, though scholars now see them more as a symptom of the era's collapse than its cause. Who were they?
Sea Peoples: Purported ancient tribal confederation of the Late Bronze Age.
Born Farid Khan, this 16th-century ruler founded an empire after defeating the Mughals and made Delhi his capital, earning the title 'the Just King' — who is he?
Sher Shah Suri: Sultan of Hindustan from 1540 to 1545.
Succeeding his father David as king of ancient Israel, this biblical ruler's wealth and foreign wives allegedly introduced idolatry, sowing the seeds for the kingdom's later split. Who is he?
Solomon: Biblical monarch of ancient Israel. The successor of his father David, he is described as the penultimate ruler of all Twelve Tribes of Israel under a united Israel and Judah.
Commonly called "SBY," this retired general was only the second military man after Suharto to become Indonesia's president, serving two terms from 2004 — who is he?

Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono: President of Indonesia from 2004 to 2014. Yudhoyono won the 2004 presidential election—the first direct presidential election in Indonesia, defeating incumbent President Megawati Sukarnoputri.
In Greek mythology, this minor deity personified death itself, and was known to the Romans as Mors or Letum — who is he?
Thanatos: Ancient Greek personification of death.

Nicknamed 'The Tiger of Malaya' after conquering the peninsula and a nearby island stronghold in just 70 days, this WWII Japanese general later held out on Luzon until his country's surrender in 1945 — who is he?
Tomoyuki Yamashita: Japanese officer and war criminal (1885–1946)
In Norse belief, these female figures guide fallen warriors to Odin's hall, sometimes shown accompanied by ravens, swans, or wolves — what are they called?
This American divorcée's romance with Britain's king forced his abdication in 1936 rather than let her become queen — who was she?
Wallis Simpson: Wife of Prince Edward, Duke of Windsor (1896–1986)

One of three brothers with distinguished military careers, this British general rose to Commander-in-Chief, America, during the War of Independence after famously scaling the cliffs at Quebec in 1759. Who was he?
William Howe, 5th Viscount Howe: British Army officer and politician (1729–1814)

Rooted in pre-Islamic Kurdish tradition and shaped by Sufi influence, this monotheistic faith reveres a 'Peacock Angel' as chief among seven angels tasked with guarding the world — which religion is it?
The eldest child of Alfred the Great, this Anglo-Saxon noblewoman ruled the Mercians in her own right from 911 until her death in 918 — who was she?
Æthelflæd: Ruler of Mercia in England from 911 to 918.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (born 1847) is the earliest of the four. Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 – March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
Which one below was established earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest release?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow is a physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Jan Baptist van Helmont is a chemist.
What is the atomic number of Carbon?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
In what year was J. Robert Oppenheimer born?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: In 1941, Oppenheimer was briefed about nuclear weapon design by Australian physicist Mark Oliphant.
In what year was Arthur Conan Doyle born?
Arthur Conan Doyle: Sir Arthur Ignatius Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 – 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
In what year was José M. Hernández born?
José M. Hernández: José Moreno Hernández (born August 7, 1962) is a Mexican-American engineer and astronaut.
In what year did Jean Tatlock die?
Jean Tatlock: Jean Frances Tatlock (February 21, 1914 – January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
In what year did Anton Chekhov die?
Anton Chekhov: Along with Henrik Ibsen and August Strindberg, Chekhov is often referred to as one of the three seminal figures in the birth of early modernism in the theatre.
In what year was Factitious disorder imposed on another discovered?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
In what year was Iridium discovered?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation
Ondansetron: Pfizer. It is also effective for treating gastroenteritis.
In which country is Minamata disease?
Minamata disease: Japan. Minamata disease (Japanese: 水俣病, Hepburn: Minamata-byō) is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning.
Who is credited with discovering Caesium?
Caesium: Robert Bunsen. Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Who is credited with discovering Nobelium?
Nobelium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Who is credited with discovering Silicon?
Silicon: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
This disorder caused by excess growth hormone after the growth plates close typically first shows up as enlarged hands and feet, followed by a bigger forehead, jaw, and nose — what is it?
Acromegaly is a disorder that results in excess growth of certain parts of the human body.
Often caused by misaligned or unevenly focused eyes in early childhood, this is the most common cause of single-eye vision loss in kids and young adults, nicknamed 'lazy eye' — what condition is it?
Amblyopia is a disorder of sight in which the brain fails to fully process input from one eye and over time favors the other eye.
This lustrous grey metalloid, found mainly in the mineral stibnite, was historically powdered for use as a cosmetic known by its Arabic name, kohl. What element is it?
Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium) and atomic number 51.

This lung condition — the partial collapse of alveoli that reduces gas exchange, usually in just one lung — is a very common finding on chest X-rays, though it's technically distinct from a fluid-filled lung or a full pneumothorax — what is it?
Atelectasis is the partial collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced or absent gas exchange, more specifically the collapse of alveoli.
This steel-gray, lightweight metal with atomic number 4 is found in gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, but within the cores of stars it gets destroyed as fast as it forms — what element is it?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
This family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, sheep, and goats across 143 living species — name the family?
Bovidae is the biological family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals that includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, and goat-antelopes such as sheep and goats.
Originating from the now-discredited caloric theory of heat, this unit of energy is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius — name the unit?
Calorie is a unit of energy that originated from the caloric theory of heat.
Discovered in 1801 by Giuseppe Piazzi and initially hailed as a new planet, this object in the main asteroid belt is now the only recognized dwarf planet orbiting within Neptune's path — what is it?
Ceres (dwarf planet) is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
After serving as dean of Harvard's Faculty of Arts and Sciences, this political scientist became the university's 30th president in July 2023 — who is she?
Claudine Gay (born August 4, 1970) is an American political scientist who is the Wilbur A. Cowett Professor of Government and of African and African-American Studies at Harvard University.
This transparent dome covering the iris and pupil provides about two-thirds of the eye's total focusing power and can be reshaped via LASIK surgery — what is it?
Cornea is the transparent front part of the eye which covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.
What unit of time, roughly 24 hours long, marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun and drives the circadian rhythms of most living things?
Day is the time period of a full rotation of the Earth with respect to the Sun.
Fossils of this Late Devonian armored fish genus, among the earliest vertebrate apex predators ever, have turned up from Morocco to Poland to North America — which genus?
Dunkleosteus is an extinct genus of large arthrodire ("jointed-neck") fish that existed during the Late Devonian period, about 382-358 million years ago.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.
Native to Mediterranean shores, this hardy perennial herb tastes much like anise and lends its flavor to absinthe; one variety swells into a bulb you can eat as a vegetable — what is it?
Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
One of Europe's smallest songbirds, this kinglet sports a bright orange-and-yellow crest in males and closely resembles the firecrest — which bird?
Goldcrest (Regulus regulus) is a very small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Confirming Maxwell's theoretical predictions, this 19th-century German physicist proved that electromagnetic waves actually exist — who is he?

Heinrich Hertz (hurts; 22 February 1857 - 1 January 1894) was a German physicist who first conclusively proved the existence of the electromagnetic waves proposed by James Clerk Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism.

This condition occurs when cerebrospinal fluid builds up in and around the brain, in babies causing a rapid increase in head size and in the elderly causing poor balance and mental decline — what condition is it?
Hydrocephalus is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) builds up within and/or around the brain, which can cause pressure to increase in the skull.

This analytical framework, which arose partly in reaction to both white feminism and the male-dominated Black liberation movement, examines how overlapping social identities create unique combinations of discrimination and privilege — name the concept?
Intersectionality is an analytical framework for understanding how groups' and individuals' social and political identities result in unique combinations of discrimination and privilege.
Holder of 128 firearm patents, this American engineer invented the telescoping bolt that made compact autoloading pistols possible — who is he?

John Browning (January 23, 1855 - November 26, 1926) was an American firearm designer who developed many varieties of military and civilian firearms, cartridges, and gun mechanisms, many of which are still in use around the world.
Named after the American endocrinologist who identified it in the 1940s, this chromosome anomaly, also called 47,XXY, typically affects phenotypic males with infertility. What condition is it?
Klinefelter syndrome (KS), also known as 47,XXY, is a chromosome anomaly.
This big-cat hybrid, born of a male lion and a female tiger, is the largest of all living cats, growing larger than either parent and enjoying a swim. What animal is it?
Liger is a hybrid offspring of a male lion (Panthera leo) and a tigress, or female tiger (Panthera tigris).

Developed by MathWorks, this proprietary programming language and numeric computing environment is built around matrix manipulation, and pairs with an add-on called Simulink for graphical simulation and model-based design. What software is this?
MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.

Designed as both fighter and ground-attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation), this all-weather supersonic, carrier-capable twin-engined jet was derived from the YF-17 and developed for the Navy. What aircraft is this?

McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation).

This synthetic prostaglandin drug can prevent stomach ulcers in people taking NSAIDs, induce labor, treat dangerous postpartum bleeding, and — alone or paired with another drug — end a pregnancy — what's the medication?

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus.

Native to the Horn of Africa and nicknamed the 'sand puppy,' this burrowing rodent is the only mammal that's a cold-blooded thermoconformer — and lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen. What is it?
Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber), also known as the sand puppy, is a burrowing rodent native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya, notably in Somali regions.
What organic molecule, composed of a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, serves as the basic building block of both DNA and RNA?
Nucleotide are organic molecules composed of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate.
This rare silvery-white metal, discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, is part of the six-element platinum group and has the lowest melting point among them. What element is it?
Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
This class of compounds is defined by a direct single bond between two oxygen atoms, denoted R−O−O−R — what are they called?
Peroxide are a group of molecules with the structure ROOR, where each R represents a radical (a portion of a complete molecule; not a free radical) and the O's are single oxygen atoms.
In Aristotle's day this kingdom included algae and fungi, but modern definitions have narrowed it to chiefly photosynthetic, mostly multicellular organisms — what is it?
Plant are the eukaryotic organisms that constitute the kingdom Plantae.

This endogenous steroid sex hormone plays a central role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development, and also serves as a key metabolic intermediate for producing other steroid hormones — name the hormone?
Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.

Cultivated mainly for its oil-rich seeds, this yellow-flowered Brassica crop is the source of a low-toxicity oil marketed under a Canadian-coined name, and ranks as the world's third-largest vegetable oil source — what is it?
Caused by two strains of human herpesvirus and nicknamed 'sixth disease,' this common childhood illness brings a rapid fever that gives way to a pink rash within days — what's it called?
Roseola is an infectious disease caused by certain types of human herpes viruses.
This marine plant group includes kelp, captures carbon, and generates over half of the planet's oxygen — what is it called?
Seaweed refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.
Doctors recommend covering your elbow rather than your hands to block this involuntary, explosive rush of air from spreading illness through the air. What is this reflex called?
Sneeze (also known as sternutation) is a semi-autonomous, convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth, usually caused by foreign particles irritating the nasal mucosa.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
A mathematics prodigy who abandoned academia in 1969 for a reclusive primitive life, he later mailed bombs over 17 years and penned a 35,000-word manifesto against modern technology — who was he?
Ted Kaczynski (k-; May 22, 1942 - June 10, 2023), also known as the Unabomber, was an American mathematician and domestic terrorist.
This metric unit of mass equals exactly 1,000 kilograms — about 2,204.6 pounds — and is technically identical to the SI unit called the megagram. What is it?
Tonne (or; symbol: t) is a unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial flowering plant is the type species of its genus and a member of the honeysuckle family — which herb?
Valerian (herb) (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
A physician, painter, and inventor, this man designed the United States Capitol and served as both the first Architect of the Capitol and the first head of the Patent Office — who was he?
William Thornton (May 20, 1759 - March 28, 1828) was an American physician, inventor, painter and architect who designed the United States Capitol.
This American psychologist devised a pyramid-shaped theory of human needs culminating in self-actualization, and was later ranked the 10th most-cited psychologist of the 20th century — who is he?

First flown as a stretched derivative of a popular narrow-body jet family in 1994, this twin-engine airliner carries up to 239 passengers and later gained a fuel-efficient 'neo' version with new winglets — which aircraft?
Airbus A321: Airliner, stretched model of the A320 family.

The brightest star in the constellation Aquila and a vertex of the Summer Triangle, this nearby A-type star spins so fast — about 286 km/s at its equator — that it bulges noticeably. Which star is it?
Altair: Brightest star in the constellation Aquila. Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky.

Affecting about 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder causes severe intellectual disability, little to no speech, and balance problems — yet those affected are often noted for a notably happy personality. Which condition is it?
Angelman syndrome: Genetic disorder caused by a mutation of chromosome 15.
Also nicknamed the cross spider or diadem spider for the white markings on its back, this orb-weaver is native to Europe but was introduced to North America — what species is it?

Araneus diadematus: Species of spider. The spider species Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.

Steel-blue with wavy black markings on its back and silvery underneath, this shoaling fish thrives in the cooler waters of the Mediterranean, Black Sea, and northern ocean near Europe — which species?
Atlantic mackerel: Species of fish. The Atlantic mackerel's body is elongate, steel-blue marked with wavy black lines dorsally and silvery-white ventrally, its snout long and pointed.

Members of the family Ursidae walk flat on plantigrade paws tipped with five claws that can't retract — and though most eat meat, the giant panda among them is mostly herbivorous. What animal is this?
Patented in 1976 and sold under the brand name Zebeta, this beta-1-selective medication treats high blood pressure and heart failure — what is it?
Bisoprolol: Beta-1 selective adrenenergic blocker medication used to treat cardiovascular diseases.
Hailing from the Anglo-Scottish frontier and frequently cited as the most intelligent dog breed on Earth, which sheepdog dominates sheepdog trials?
Border Collie: Working dog breed. The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size.
This condition involves inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that normally cushion friction near joints like the shoulder, elbow, hip and knee — what is it?
Bursitis: Inflammation of the bursae (sacs of synovial fluid in joints)
Native to the Americas, this plant genus in the nightshade family produces the fruits we call peppers, including sweet bell types and fiery chilies — what genus is it?
This bacterial skin infection affects the dermis and subcutaneous fat, most often striking the legs or face and causing spreading redness and swelling — what is it?
Cellulitis: Bacterial infection of the inner layers of the skin called the dermis.

A yellowish-green gas that turns reddish-brown liquid when cooled and bright orange crystals when colder still, this compound is usually handled in solution and used as a bleach and disinfectant — what is it?
This French inventor born near Toulouse is remembered chiefly as an aviation pioneer, but in 1870 he was also among the first to take up the sport of cycling in France — who is it?
Clément Ader: French inventor and engineer (1841–1925)
Better known as "pink eye," this inflammation of the clear layer over the white of the eye can leave a lid stuck shut by morning — what's the medical name?

Conjunctivitis: Inflammation of the eye. Conjunctivitis, also known as pink eye, is inflammation of the conjunctiva, the thin and clear layer that covers the white surface of the eye and the inner eyelid.
Commonly called comb jellies, these are the largest animals that swim using rows of cilia, drifting through every ocean as masses of two-layered jelly — what's the phylum?
Ctenophora: Phylum of gelatinous marine animals.
From muntjac to moose, members of the family Cervidae shed and regrow bony skull extensions each year — antlers used to battle rivals. What hoofed ruminant is this?
Deer: Family of hoofed mammals. A deer (pl.: deer) or true deer is a hoofed ruminant ungulate of the family Cervidae (informally the deer family).
Bred around 1890 by a Thuringian tax collector looking for a loyal guard dog, this sleek, high-alert German breed traditionally had its ears cropped and tail docked — which breed?
Dobermann: Black and tan dog breed from Germany.
Having studied mathematics under Karl Weierstrass, which philosopher founded the school of phenomenology and argued that transcendental consciousness sets the limits of all possible knowledge?
Coiled to just 6 to 7 centimetres but stretching nearly 20 feet if unraveled, this tube connects each testicle to the vas deferens and stores maturing sperm — what is it?

Epididymis: Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens. The epididymis serves as an interconnection between the multiple efferent ducts at the rear of a testicle (proximally), and the vas deferens (distally).
The most widely distributed member of its subfamily, this semiaquatic, fish-eating mustelid ranges across Europe, much of Asia, and North Africa's Maghreb — which animal?
Reproducing via spores rather than seeds or flowers, this group of vascular plants unfurls from coiled 'fiddleheads' into fronds and numbers over 10,000 species — what are they?
Fern: Class of vascular plants. The group includes about 10,560 known extant species.
Alongside James Watson, this English scientist co-authored the 1953 Nature paper unveiling DNA's double helix and later coined the phrase 'central dogma' — who is he?
Francis Crick: English physicist and biologist (1916–2004)

Born as an air-superiority day fighter and now, as of 2026, the world's most common military fixed-wing aircraft with over 4,600 built, this single-engine jet flies on as the 'Viper' family — which aircraft?
General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon: American multi-role fighter aircraft.
Dubbed the 'king of the birds' in European folklore for its golden head crest, this tiny kinglet's scientific name literally means 'petty king' — which bird?
Goldcrest: Small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.

This French mathematician, famous for his work in algebraic topology, came from an almost absurdly mathematical dynasty: son of mathematician Élie, nephew of mathematician Anna, and brother to a composer, a physicist, and yet another mathematician — who was he?
This small rodent, pointed-snouted with large rounded ears, has become the standard laboratory model organism after thriving alongside human settlements — what is it?
This physical phenomenon describes how a system's current state depends on its past history, forming looping curves in magnets and giving hard disk drives their memory — what is it?
Hysteresis: Dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.
This condition restricts blood flow to tissue, starving cells of oxygen and nutrients due to causes like thrombosis or embolism — what's it called?
Ischemia: Restriction in blood supply to tissues.
This British chemical engineer founded a major chemicals group in 1998 and later became a minority shareholder with control over football operations at Manchester United — who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe: British engineer and businessman (born 1952)
Its subfamily name literally means 'large foot,' it's native to Australia and New Guinea, and a 2019 government tally counted some 42.8 million of them in harvest areas. Which marsupial?
Kangaroo: Marsupial of the family Macropodidae.
This is the most abundant genus of trees on Earth, dominating the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada despite dropping its needles every fall. What genus is it?
Larch: Genus of deciduous conifers in the family Pinaceae.

Nicknamed the 'leopard slug' for its spotted grey-brown skin, this mollusc mates by dangling from a thread of mucus off a tree branch — which species, first spotted outside Europe in Philadelphia in 1867?
Limax maximus: Species of slug. It is among the largest keeled slugs, Limax cinereoniger being the largest.
As West Germany's economics minister, he engineered the postwar 'Wirtschaftswunder' before becoming the country's second chancellor in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard: Chancellor of West Germany from 1963 to 1966.

Despite its fox-like markings, this leggy, reddish-coated canine of the South American savanna is neither a fox nor a close relative of more familiar canines, and it plays a key role dispersing fruit seeds — what is it?

Co-inventor of a heart-valve repair device called the MitraClip, this Turkish-American cardiac surgeon became a famous TV health personality before being named the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in 2025 — who is he?
Mehmet Oz: American TV host and government official (born 1960)
Sitting atop the brainstem and linking it to the diencephalon and cerebrum, this structure governs vision, hearing, motor control, and arousal -- what is it called?
Midbrain: Forward-most portion of the brainstem.
The platypus and the four species of echidna are the only living mammals in this order that lay eggs rather than bear live young — what is it called?

Dropped from a B-52 and boosted by a modified Pegasus rocket stage before its own scramjet took over, this experimental hypersonic craft still holds the record for fastest jet-powered flight at about Mach 9.6 — what is it?
NASA X-43: Unmanned US experimental hypersonic aircraft, 1991-2000.

Named for a mythological daughter of Tantalus, this silvery transition metal with atomic number 41 was once called columbium and is now prized as a nickel-free option in hypoallergenic jewelry — which element?
Niobium: Chemical element with atomic number 41 (Nb)
This English physicist identified electromagnetic radiation independently of Hertz and built an early radio receiver he named the "coherer" — who was he?
Oliver Lodge: English physicist and electrical engineer (1851–1940)
Discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, this silvery-white platinum-group metal is prized for cleaning up automobile exhaust in catalytic converters — which element?
Palladium: Chemical element with atomic number 46 (Pd)
This psychiatric paraphilia involves a primary or exclusive sexual attraction to prepubescent children, with diagnostic criteria extending the cutoff age to thirteen — which disorder?
Pedophilia: Sexual attraction to prepubescent children. The DSM requires the arousal pattern must be present for 6 months or longer, while the ICD lacks this requirement.
This branch of linguistics studies how spoken languages organize meaningful sound units — the kind of contrast that separates 'bat' from 'gnat' — what field is it?
Phonology: Study of sound organization in languages.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.
Built with a ribless cartilage skeleton, skin-covering dermal denticles and five to seven gill slits per side, these fish first appeared back in the Devonian — what are they?
A hygroscopic crystalline powder (formula NaNO2) and the most industrially important salt of its kind, this compound is most familiar to us cured into processed meats. What is it?
Sodium nitrite: Chemical compound. It is a white to slightly yellowish crystalline powder that is very soluble in water and is hygroscopic.
This Polish-American DuPont chemist invented a super-strong polymer fiber and became the fourth woman ever inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame — who was she?
Stephanie Kwolek: American chemist who invented Kevlar (1923–2014)
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
